channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Wet and windy start to Tuesday across Essex, with gusts close to 40mph
item.description: The heaviest rain is forecast in the early hours, before the wind peaks in the morning and brighter weather arrives on Wednesday.

item.title: Police searching for missing Grays man Patrick Francisco, 83
item.description: Officers say they are worried about the pensioner, who has not been seen since Monday afternoon.

item.title: Colchester councillors to weigh up major spending plan for Leisure World
item.description: Colchester City Council leaders are taking plans to the council's cabinet for what they call the biggest investment in Leisure World for a generation.

item.title: Three taxis taken off the road after police checks at Harlow station
item.description: Officers in Harlow stopped 62 taxis and private hire vehicles at the railway station and found most of them in order.

item.title: Essex pupils to shape year-long county push against bullying
item.description: Essex County Council has launched Let's Talk... Safe Relationships across Essex, built with the Young Essex Assembly and the Multi-Schools Council.

item.title: Rosie the Jack Russell is dug out of a Maldon rabbit hole and learns absolutely nothing
item.description: Firefighters cleared trees and dug with great care to free the terrier, who bolted for the next burrow the moment she was out.

item.title: Spanish fashion chain Mango heading for Chelmsford's High Chelmer centre
item.description: Mango plans a new store in the High Chelmer shopping centre in Chelmsford city centre, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Lung cancer screening arrives in Harlow, the first town in west Essex to get it
item.description: Current and former smokers in Harlow are being invited for free checks that can find the disease before any symptoms appear, NHS Essex says.

item.title: Power back on in Chelmer Village and Springfield after underground cable fault
item.description: UK Power Networks reconnected the last homes by 5pm, after a high voltage fault left part of east Chelmsford without electricity for about three hours.

item.title: Police concerned for missing Clacton girl Hannah Steer, 15
item.description: She has not been seen since about 9.30pm on Sunday, and Essex Police says officers need to find her to make sure she is ok.

item.title: Free parking returns to selected Southend council car parks in December
item.description: Southend-on-Sea City Council says free festive parking will come back in some of its car parks across the city to help local shops before Christmas.

item.title: St Luke's Hospice bistro launches its first Christmas menu
item.description: SEASONS @ St Luke's, the hospice bistro created with MasterChef finalist Anurag Aggarwal, serves festive meals on weekdays from 1 to 24 December.

item.title: Havens Hospices asks Essex to back its Big Yes! Christmas appeal
item.description: The charity that runs Fair Havens and Little Havens Children's Hospice says £31 could pay for an hour of specialist nursing care over Christmas.

item.title: Orsett Hospital clinics moved out before winter as heating fails
item.description: X-ray, orthopaedic and ear, nose and throat services are leaving the ageing Thurrock hospital, and there is no new home yet for its eye and kidney clinics.

item.title: Alresford bowel cancer survivor walks 45 miles for research
item.description: Nina Murton from Alresford, diagnosed with bowel cancer in 2016, has raised almost £600 for the Bowelbabe Fund for Cancer Research UK, walking mostly along the creek to Wivenhoe in October.

item.title: Colchester Local Plan heads for the inspector after more than 1,800 responses
item.description: Colchester City Council's draft Local Plan, which sets where new homes and jobs go across the city, could be sent for independent examination once a committee reviews the public's comments.

item.title: Man arrested at Maldon home where officers were searching for missing man
item.description: The missing man was not there, but police found someone at the address wanted for previous offences, whose behaviour then became concerning.

item.title: Dunmow Road into Thaxted shut for Essex Highways roadworks, with a long diversion for drivers
item.description: Essex Highways has closed Dunmow Road, the route in and out of Thaxted, for roadworks, leaving drivers facing lengthy delays and a long way round.

item.title: Public inquiry into land for Chelmsford's £81m Army and Navy scheme opens next week
item.description: A government-appointed inspector will hear objections to the land deals and road changes Essex County Council needs to replace the Army and Navy roundabout in Chelmsford.

item.title: Home Office asks ministers, not Braintree council, to approve longer life for Wethersfield asylum centre
item.description: Braintree District Council's leader called the application for the former airfield near Wethersfield incredibly disappointing and said the council will take legal advice on any decision to extend it.

item.title: Nine trees to come down on Chelmsford's North Avenue after safety inspection
item.description: Chelmsford City Council found defects in trees near homes, roads and two primary schools on North Avenue, and is carrying out work on many more of them.

item.title: Harlow's Water Gardens to host Mind in West Essex's fifth Merry Minds fun run
item.description: A festive 5km for walkers, joggers and runners in Harlow will raise money for a mental health charity whose funds all stay in west Essex.

item.title: Southend Airport wins daily Zurich flights with Swiss carrier Chair Airlines
item.description: Flights from London Southend Airport to Switzerland's largest city start on 27 May 2027 and run all year, with tickets on sale from 16 November 2026.

item.title: Inspector overrules Maldon council to allow self-build house on Tollesbury field
item.description: A planning inspector gave the go-ahead for a two-bedroom home beyond Tollesbury's village boundary, citing Maldon District's shortfall in housing land.

item.title: Silt cleared from five Harlow ponds in first wave of restoration
item.description: Harlow Council has started work on five of the town's 18 ponds, including Church End, Harlow Common and Mill Street, to help wildlife and improve green spaces.

item.title: Footage shows stolen BMW tearing through M25 roadworks at Theydon as Roadworker Safety Week begins
item.description: Road workers at the M25 Theydon interchange near Epping were missed by inches when a stolen car burst through a temporary barrier, and two brothers on the crew have now told the BBC about it.

item.title: Auditors expect to give no opinion on three years of Basildon Council's accounts
item.description: Basildon Borough Council's external auditors, EY, told councillors that the 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26 accounts are all expected to receive disclaimed opinions, and listed borrowing, Sempra Homes and housing among areas of significant risk.

item.title: Basildon Council borrowing stands at £727m as sale of its Dartford investment property is delayed
item.description: Basildon Borough Council's leader told the Audit and Risk Committee he does not support adding to the council's long-term debt until the Dartford property is sold.

item.title: Southend cabinet backs £800,000 plan to remove Three Shells Lagoon
item.description: Southend-on-Sea City Council's cabinet agreed on 16 November to clear the fenced-off lagoon beside Southend Pier and return the site to natural beach, a decade after it was built for nearly £2m.

item.title: Nearly 100 Colchester households stuck in B&Bs as emergency housing demand climbs
item.description: Officers warn the city's homelessness budget will be heavily overspent this year as more families are placed in temporary homes.

item.title: Essex Police can now bar high-risk drink and drug driving suspects from driving while on bail
item.description: Across Essex, suspects who cannot be charged straight away can be released on condition they stay off the roads until their case is decided.

item.title: Chelmsford Chieftains beat Slough Jets 6-3 with a strong final period
item.description: Lane Paddison broke a 3-3 deadlock early in the third period as the Chelmsford club won game five of their Challenge Cup campaign at Riverside Ice and Leisure.

item.title: Chelmsford pupils turn archaeologist as museum sends Iron Age gold hoard box into schools
item.description: The Museum of Chelmsford has built a new loan box for primary schools around the Great Baddow Coin Hoard, with help from local pupils and teachers.

item.title: Cheshunt man, 41, charged with arson over two Waltham Abbey shop fires
item.description: Shorish Mahmoud, of Maple Lane, is due before Chelmsford magistrates on Wednesday 9 December.

item.title: Missing Wickford man Simon Mahoney found safe, Essex Police say
item.description: Officers had widened the search beyond Essex after he was caught on CCTV in Chelmsford shops on Friday.

item.title: Rim Jhim Spice in Stanway takes top national curry restaurant title
item.description: The Stanway curry house near Colchester has been named Restaurant of the Year at the National Curry Awards, with its trophy presented at the House of Lords.

item.title: Two men arrested after man suffers facial injuries in Saffron Walden's Market Row
item.description: Essex Police are appealing for information after a man in his 30s was taken to hospital following an assault in Saffron Walden town centre.

item.title: Maldon Salt mixes German rock salt into its product, Observer finds
item.description: Lorries delivering bulk bags of mined salt were filmed at the firm's Goldhanger works. Regulators say the product is legally labelled.

item.title: Essex Police secure more than 200 shop theft charges in a fortnight as retailers report more
item.description: Fifty people were charged in two weeks across the county, many of them in court the next day.

item.title: More than 100 people from many faiths gather at Grays gurdwara for Thurrock's fifth interfaith conference
item.description: Councillors, police leaders and representatives of many religions joined the event in Grays, organised by Thurrock councillor Qaisar Abbas.

item.title: Harlow Council to put up Christmas trees in five neighbourhood shopping areas
item.description: Trees will appear at The Stow, Old Harlow, Bush Fair, Churchgate Street and Potter Street, with residents and traders helping.

item.title: Essex firefighters offer free car checks with Halfords, starting at Colchester fire station
item.description: Essex County Fire and Rescue Service has teamed up with Halfords to run free 360-degree vehicle checks at fire stations across the county during Road Safety Week.

item.title: New image in bid to name man found dead at Southend East 26 years ago
item.description: Locate International hopes a forensic artist's picture of 'Southend Station Man' as he may have looked around 1980 will be recognised by someone who knew him then.

item.title: Churchgoers across the Diocese of Chelmsford asked to help shape an independent safeguarding audit
item.description: An anonymous online survey for people involved in local churches is open until 8 December, ahead of a review of the diocese and Chelmsford Cathedral early in 2027.

item.title: BASICS Essex volunteer doctors and paramedics win the King's Award for Voluntary Service
item.description: The Essex emergency medical charity, founded in 1973, is one of six Essex groups among 250 honoured across the UK on Saturday 14 November 2026.

item.title: Man of no fixed abode charged with two counts of assault by beating in Harlow
item.description: Denzel Barzey, 32, has appeared before magistrates in Chelmsford accused of assaulting a man in Harlow in May.

item.title: Harlow parkrun marks 12 years with MP Chris Vince among the runners
item.description: Harlow's weekly 5k parkrun in the town park held its 558th event as it celebrated a dozen years since its first outing.

item.title: Thurrock families could get travel budgets in place of council taxis for SEND students
item.description: Thurrock Council is consulting until 24 December on changes to home-to-school transport, and says no decisions have been made.

item.title: Teenage boy wounded by air rifle in Chadwell St Mary street
item.description: Armed officers went to the scene in Chadwell St Mary, and Essex Police say they are following a number of targeted lines of enquiry.

item.title: Essex & Herts Air Ambulance calls on more women doctors and paramedics to join its helicopter crews
item.description: Women are still a minority in helicopter emergency medicine across the UK, and the charity's flight doctor Kate Jackson has a simple message for anyone who doubts she belongs: apply.

item.title: Brentwood's town centre business group and its art trail up for national awards
item.description: Brentwood Connected, the business improvement district for Brentwood, Shenfield and Ingatestone, is a finalist in two categories at the National BID Awards.

item.title: Home Bargains wants to take over empty TUI unit and double its Basildon store
item.description: TJ Morris, which runs the chain, has asked Basildon Council to knock its Westgate Shopping Park shop through into the unit next door.

item.title: Driver counts 15 dead animals along two miles of the A120
item.description: A motorist told BBC News she counted the carcasses on a single short stretch of the A120 across north Essex, raising questions over what can be done about deer killed on the road.

item.title: Learn the 4Ts: Rayleigh mother shares her daughter's intensive care ordeal so parents spot type 1 diabetes sooner
item.description: Mandy was told to prepare for the worst when Zara, then 13, reached Southend Hospital. Months of warning signs had gone unnoticed.

item.title: Billericay Town beat Waltham Abbey to stay in the FA Trophy as Braintree Town and Aveley go out
item.description: Billericay are the last Essex club left in non-league's national knockout competition, after a weekend that ended the cup hopes of Braintree, Aveley and Chelmsford City.

item.title: Southend United fight back to beat ten-man Aldershot Town 2-1 at Roots Hall
item.description: Second-half goals from Kyle McAdam and Tyreece Simpson kept Southend in the National League play-off places.

item.title: Isthmian North: Canvey Island hit five at Witham Town as Bowers & Pitsea win at Concord Rangers
item.description: It was a strong Saturday for Essex sides on the road, with Tilbury and Brightlingsea Regent also collecting away wins.

item.title: Chelmsford City knocked out of the FA Trophy on penalties at AFC Telford United
item.description: The Clarets were beaten 6-5 in a shootout in Shropshire despite two saves from goalkeeper Marriott.

item.title: Javelin great Fatima Whitbread made a Freewoman of Brentwood for her work with children in care
item.description: The former world champion, who grew up in children's homes, is the borough's newest honorary freewoman, just over a year after Thurrock gave her its own freedom.

item.title: Colchester United end 10-game winless run by beating Gillingham 2-0
item.description: Two goals inside nine second-half minutes at the JobServe Community Stadium lifted the mood in Colchester after weeks without a win.
